contract.note: A URL open, search query, or click counts as one logical operation. A shared source open is recorded once and reused across report origins. No project execution or source edits were performed.

sources.content: Full article text accessible on a third-party uploaded mirror; original publisher page was not readable. Title/abstract at lines 41-58 identifies finite noisy discrete-time observations, CR bounds, DFT-related ML algorithms and threshold analysis; the paper's single-tone/independent Gaussian-noise assumptions are stated around lines 61-66. Further text supports periodogram/global-maximum and threshold/outlier discussion.
sources.publication: IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 20(5), 591-598 (1974) publication corroborated by bibliographic records; peer-review status not independently verified from accessible primary/institutional evidence.
sources.verification: Content support is usable with the mirror provenance limitation; numeric bounds and transfer to the hypothetical receiver remain unverified.

sources.content: Institutional repository abstract, lines 28-30: single complex sinusoid in complex white Gaussian noise; more computationally efficient than optimal ML and as good at moderately high SNR. Citation at lines 31-45 identifies IEEE journal, volume, issue and pages.
sources.publication: Journal article publication verified by institutional citation; peer-review status not explicitly established on the accessible record.
sources.verification: Abstract-limited support only; no full derivation or low-SNR/receiver-specific performance verified.

sources.content: IEEE publisher search result abstract: generalized Kay/differential-phase estimator for a single complex sinusoid in complex AWGN; arbitrary delay, variance/range/complexity comparisons; delay two approaches CRB asymptotically at high SNR as sequence length grows.
sources.publication: IEEE Transactions on Communications 54(3), 407-415 (2006) metadata verified in publisher search result; article page returned HTTP 418; peer-review status not separately verified.
sources.verification: Abstract-limited; page fetch failed, and source assumptions do not establish continuity or suitability for the receiver.

sources.content: IEEE publisher result abstract: for sinusoidal frequency estimation in additive white Gaussian noise, threshold effect occurs when Barankin bound significantly departs from CRB; SNR*T/ln(T) is described as an indicator in the studied model.
sources.publication: IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing 45(9), 2398-2401 (1997) metadata verified by publisher result; page fetch returned HTTP 418; peer-review status not separately verified.
sources.verification: Abstract-limited. The indicator is model-specific and is not a threshold calculation for this task.

sources.content: Institutional repository abstract, lines 17-20: complex sinusoid with multiplicative and additive complex noise; multiplicative noise smears the spectral line and may degrade accuracy; analyzes finite-sample CRBs, coherent/noncoherent SNR and covariance-angle estimators.
sources.publication: Repository identifies IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing 49(4), 777-789 (2001), lines 14-16; peer-review status not separately verified.
sources.verification: Abstract-limited; supports the stated Doppler-spread caveat but does not establish equivalence to this receiver's drift or envelope.

sources.content: IEEE publisher search result abstract: high-SNR additive noise is treated as equivalent phase noise; phase linear regression estimates frequency/phase with CR-bound variances; frequency variance formula depends on noise power spectrum.
sources.publication: IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 31(6), 832-835 (1985) metadata verified by publisher result; direct open returned the JavaScript/robot page; peer-review status not separately verified.
sources.verification: Abstract-limited; no full text was retrieved.

sources.content: IEEE publisher search result abstract: approximate time-domain ML under reasonably high SNR uses noisy-sample phase and magnitude; phase alone is not sufficient; proposes recursive phase unwrapping.
sources.publication: IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing 55(3), 834-845 (2007) metadata verified by publisher result; direct open returned the JavaScript/robot page; peer-review status not separately verified.
sources.verification: Abstract-limited; result is conditional on the paper's single-sinusoid AWGN model and high-SNR premise.

sources.content: Publisher abstract, lines 60-63: a linear two-state phase/frequency Kalman filter uses measured carrier phase; reports acquisition within 10 symbols at stated offset/C/N in its digital-carrier setting. The linked PDF was not inspected in this verification.
sources.publication: Official J-STAGE record identifies IEEJ Transactions on Electronics, Information and Systems 123(10), 1735-1744, 2003, and gives published date at lines 27-35; peer-review status not stated.
sources.verification: Abstract-limited support; reported acquisition result is specific to its signal, symbol, offset and C/N setup.

sources.content: Full author preprint accessible. Lines 58-60 caution that large multi-frequency periodogram values do not prove every modeled sinusoidal component is present; lines 359-360 qualify an upper-bound approximation under stated assumptions. The paper develops false-alarm/significance treatment for searched frequency tuples.
sources.publication: The arXiv record supplies the full author preprint; MNRAS 436, 807-818 (2013) is identified by publisher bibliographic search result, but the publisher page could not be opened in the original report. Peer-review status not independently verified here.
sources.verification: Full preprint content supports a scan-level significance discriminator, but not a false-alarm formula for this receiver's noise, band, repeated looks or stateful decision logic.

original_findings.source_content: full via third-party mirror plus abstracts
original_findings.publication_status: journal publication verified; peer review unknown
original_findings.caveat: Rife/Boorstyn supports a threshold effect and its full mirror discusses wrong-maximum/outlier behavior; Barankin abstract supports threshold departure from CRB for its sinusoid/AWGN model. Neither maps threshold to the hypothetical C/N0 or receiver.
original_findings.reason: Separating tails/acquisition failures from local variance and uncertainty is a relevant validation decision.

original_findings.publication_status: journal publication verified; peer review unknown
original_findings.caveat: Kay's result is limited to a complex sinusoid in complex white Gaussian noise at moderately high SNR.
original_findings.reason: The proposed matched block-estimator benchmark is actionable without claiming it wins.

original_findings.publication_status: journal publication verified; peer review unknown
original_findings.caveat: Delay-dependent variance and range/complexity tradeoffs are supported at abstract level; continuous phase across apertures is an external requirement, not established by this source.
original_findings.reason: A small delay sweep with explicit reset controls can discriminate a plausible estimator option.

original_findings.publication_status: journal publication verified; peer review unknown
original_findings.caveat: Doppler spreading is modeled as multiplicative noise; it may not match the receiver's oscillator drift or amplitude behavior.
original_findings.reason: Comparing stationary and controlled time-varying captures tests whether longer coherent support helps.

deduplicated_union.finding: Threshold/outlier risk makes local variance or a finite uncertainty field insufficient for acquisition qualification.
Use a computationally light single-tone block estimator as a measured baseline.
Differential-phase delay trades estimation variance against range/complexity.
Doppler/multiplicative variation can smear a line and change the benefit of longer integration.

strict_prefix_eligibility.first_violating_operation: Operation 17: click of the J-STAGE PDF link. This was followed by a DOI click, arXiv full-text open (operation 19), and a further IEEE open (operation 20). The full Baluev text was therefore unavailable within the strict prefix. The first 16 operations provide report-level abstracts/metadata for Rife, Kay and J-STAGE; A4 had publisher/search leads and a failed OUP page open but no opened full source. Treat F4 as unresolved in strict-prefix scoring (qualified-count lower bound 3, upper bound 4); do not count the post-prefix full-text advantage there.

deduplicated_union.finding: Threshold/outlier risk makes local CRB/uncertainty insufficient for acquisition qualification.
A simple complex-tone block estimator can be used as a matched baseline.
A recursive phase/frequency estimator is an option only if phase observations are trustworthy.
A searched multi-frequency maximum needs scan-level significance/presence validation.

case_results.omissions_and_errors: The report correctly left peer review unverified. Its original operation list has 20 logical operations: operations 17-20 are beyond the 16-operation total ceiling, and operations 19-20 also put the total open/click count above 10. The 8-query ceiling is met exactly at the strict prefix. The original report itself notes the overrun.

original_findings.publication_status: journal publication corroborated; peer review unknown
original_findings.caveat: The paper supports low-SNR threshold/outlier behavior under finite single-tone independent Gaussian noise; no proposed C/N0, error target or capture-rate claim is transferred.
original_findings.reason: Empirical tail, outlier and false-publication measurements are more informative than local variance alone.

original_findings.publication_status: journal publication verified; peer review unknown
original_findings.caveat: Tretter's high-SNR phase-regression premise and MAP/ML's reasonably-high-SNR complex-sample model are stated; Kay's abstract gives a moderately-high-SNR white-noise comparison. None addresses receiver modulation, envelope, reset path or uncertainty calibration.
original_findings.reason: Phase-only versus magnitude-weighted matched captures with explicit continuity/reset controls are a concrete option discriminator.

original_findings.publication_status: journal publication corroborated; peer review unknown
original_findings.caveat: Finite-record/global-search evidence supports distinguishing aperture from delivery chunking conceptually; actual callback continuity and project runtime behavior are not established by the paper.
original_findings.reason: Replaying identical PCM/timestamps with different delivery partitions can distinguish transport chunking from signal discontinuity.

deduplicated_union.finding: Low-SNR global-search outliers need empirical tail and false-publication checks.
Phase-only and amplitude-weighted/complex estimators have different assumptions and should be compared on matched inputs.
Observation aperture and delivery chunk size are different variables if original sample timing is retained.
